title: Sultanate of Terengganu
capsule: The Sultanate of Terengganu on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula was established in 1724 under Sultan Zainal Abidin I, a prince of the Johor-Riau sultanate, making it one of the last independent Malay sultanates to emerge. The state enjoyed silk and pepper commerce along the South China Sea coast and maintained varying degrees of tributary relations with Siam. In 1909, under the Anglo-Siamese Treaty, Britain transferred Siamese suzerainty rights over Terengganu to the crown, and a British Adviser was imposed in 1919, ending the sultanate's practical independence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Terengganu's coastal territorial extent is well documented from British colonial records after 1909; the pre-protectorate inland boundaries are poorly mapped and a matter of approximation.
